title: Uptime Service Credits on Web Hosting Plans
content:
Service level terms — uptime credits on Web Hosting Plans.

**Credit.** When a plan's measured uptime for a calendar month is below the tier's uptime commitment, the customer may claim a service credit of the tier's per-step percentage of the monthly fee for each started 0.1 percentage point of shortfall, capped at the tier's monthly cap percentage. The monthly fee is the amount of the line that paid the term covering that month divided by that line's term months, before any credit. The credit is the monthly fee multiplied by the lesser of the cap percentage and the per-step percentage multiplied by the started steps, divided by 100, rounded half up to the cent; the started steps are the number of started 0.1 percentage points by which the measured uptime falls short of the commitment.

**Claim window.** An uptime credit may be claimed only on or before the last day of the affected calendar month plus the tier's claim days in calendar days. The window adds whole calendar days to the month's last day, counting the next day as day 1, and the last day is included. The month and its measured uptime are those of the plan's published uptime report.

**Issue.** One credit is issued per plan per calendar month, it is added to account credit as a service credit, rounded half up to the cent, and it is never paid out to a card. Months in which the plan was suspended for any reason earn no credit.

**Worked examples (hypothetical figures).**

1. Line of USD 287.64 paying a 12-month term: monthly fee USD 23.97. Commitment 99.9 percent, measured 99.62 percent: shortfall 0.28 points, three started steps, at 5 percent each 15 percent; credit USD 3.60.
2. Same plan measured at 98.70 percent: twelve started steps would give 60 percent, so the cap of 50 percent applies; credit USD 11.99 (half of 23.97 is 11.985, rounded half up).
3. Affected month June with a 30-day claim window: the last claim day is 30 July.
